title: Welcome a guest
task: Welcome a guest: explore four specific source accounts through playable design interpretations.
notice: Source-informed accounts; no community endorsement. Interactive assets are not included in this archive export.

scenes.title: A table set for talking
scenes.scope: Turkish coffee hospitality in Fulya Ozerkan’s Istanbul account, including attributed coffee specialists; not all households in Türkiye.
scenes.context: This scene draws on Fulya Ozerkan’s UNESCO Courier article about Turkish coffee, including an account from coffee specialist Cenk Girginol. The article connects coffee with conversation and describes a cezve, a small cup and saucer, and water served alongside. Here, arranging a fictional table makes space for three people to talk. The placement puzzle belongs to this design; it does not teach a required serving order or describe every household in Türkiye.
scenes.interpretation: Place the objects so three imagined people can share one table; any layout is a design choice.
scenes.uncertainty: One journalistic account with named contributors. Household, regional and diaspora practices vary. No community review; no universal serving order asserted.

sources.title: Turkish coffee, not just a drink but a culture
sources.author: Fulya Ozerkan; includes Cenk Girginol’s account

scenes.title: Three cups, even attention
scenes.scope: Ye Hanzhong’s Chaozhou gongfu cha teaching account at Chengnan Middle School, Guangdong, reported in December 2025.
scenes.context: This scene follows an attributed teaching account, rather than a general account of Chinese hospitality. In Li Yingxue’s report from Chaozhou, practitioner Ye Hanzhong explains preparation, brewing and sharing, including distributing tea among three cups for a host and two guests. The playable pouring controls make that attention visible. They simplify a skilled practice into a diagram; the numerical fill levels and button sequence are invented interface mechanics, not technical brewing instructions.
scenes.interpretation: Pour invented diagram levels across three cups; matching levels show attention, not skill or a recipe.
scenes.uncertainty: One reported practitioner account, not all gongfu cha practices. Diagram omits heat, timing, utensil preparation and trained technique. No community review.

sources.title: A lesson steeped in tradition
sources.author: Li Yingxue; interview with practitioner Ye Hanzhong

scenes.title: Cool water, shared space
scenes.scope: UNESCO’s account of Tereré in Pohã Ñana traditions in Paraguay and their Guaraní-rooted heritage; not every Paraguayan or Guaraní practice.
scenes.context: UNESCO’s account of Tereré in Pohã Ñana traditions describes cold-water preparation, yerba mate and a bombilla, alongside family transmission and social connection. Its scope is a Guaraní-rooted heritage practice in Paraguay, not a single way that everyone welcomes visitors. This scene reveals preparation objects and a shared space. Its reveal order is invented. It offers no herb identification, medicinal advice, health claim or instruction to share drinking equipment; those questions need situated knowledge and care.
scenes.interpretation: Players reveal objects one by one around a shared table; the order is an invented game choice, not a ritual or sharing instruction.
scenes.uncertainty: Institutional heritage account; no practitioner review of this adaptation. No medicinal efficacy, plant identification, hygiene or fixed sharing etiquette asserted.

sources.title: Practices and traditional knowledge of Terere in the culture of Pohã Ñana, Guaraní ancestral drink in Paraguay
sources.author: UNESCO inscription account, nomination submitted by Paraguay

scenes.title: A pause with room to share
scenes.scope: Visit Sweden’s contemporary visitor account of fika at home, work and cafés; not a prescription for Swedish people.
scenes.context: Visit Sweden presents fika as a chance to pause and connect, often around coffee and something sweet. Its visitor guide describes flexible timing and settings, including home, work and cafés, rather than a strict ceremony. This scene invites a pause in a fictional visit. The expanding space and optional timer are interface inventions: they do not measure authentic fika, require coffee, or imply that all Swedish people enjoy the same routine.
scenes.interpretation: Players widen a shared table space at their own pace; the optional timer and spacing are design inventions, not cultural rules.
scenes.uncertainty: Tourism account, not a survey or community review. Fika can vary and can be solitary. No mandatory food, duration, setting or social rule asserted.
